**For most buyers, LiFePO4 is the better choice.** Most sources agree on this, and the newest mid-size and large models almost all use it.

**Why LiFePO4 usually wins**
- **Cycle life:** The sources rate LiFePO4 units at roughly 3,000 to 6,000 cycles to 80% capacity. NMC units are typically rated lower, from about 500 to 1,000 or 2,000 cycles ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/learn/lifepo4-vs-nmc), [VoltVanguard](https://volt-vanguard.com/article/lifepo4-vs-nmc-battery-chemistry/)). Daily use makes this difference matter most.
- **Safety:** In the lab studies the sources cite, LFP cells ran hotter less often and failed less violently than NMC cells. LFP is not fireproof, though ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Cost per cycle:** The price gap has mostly closed. Because LFP lasts longer, it usually works out cheaper per cycle ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Where NMC still makes sense**
- **Weight:** NMC stores more energy per pound at the cell level. In finished stations, though, the gap is smaller, often around 10–16% per pound, because the inverter, case, and ports weigh the same either way ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Light use:** A unit used a few weekends a year may never hit its cycle limit, so NMC can be a reasonable buy at a discount.
- **Units you already own:** If an NMC station still works, there's no need to replace it ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).

**Caveats on the numbers**
- Cycle ratings aren't directly comparable. A rating "to 70%" promises less than one "to 80%," and test conditions vary by brand. Check the spec sheet for the end point ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- Charging temperature limits depend on the maker, not the chemistry. Most LiFePO4 stations won't charge below 32°F (0°C) ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
